description: Phase-OP+ — 6-story extension of Phase-OP (memory/learning loop). Closes the 'Aura learns by herself' loop with security + decay + dedup + post-turn hooks + priority pinning + pre-call validation. All 6 open decisions locked 2026-05-19 per docs/phase-op-plus-plan-2026-05-19.md §5. Sources: docs/phase-op-plus-{plan,mem0-research,openhuman-research,web-research}-2026-05-19.md. Predecessor: Phase-OP (US-OP01..05, 660531da..71bbb003). After this closes, Aura learns from N-failure patterns (US-OP07), pins Critical/High lessons (US-OP09), dedups contradictions (US-OP06), rejects memory-poisoning attempts (US-OP10), decays stale Normal lessons (US-OP11), and catches parameter mistakes BEFORE dispatch (US-OP12). Order: security-first (US-OP10 priority=1), then post-hook learning (US-OP07), priority pinning (US-OP09), LLM judge (US-OP06), decay (US-OP11), precall validator (US-OP12). US-OP12 added 2026-05-19 from Aura's own self-diagnosis in conversation (id 4417). ~6 sessions, ~2550 LOC net new.

userStories.title: Memory-poisoning defense — provenance gate + content sanitizer + quarantine UI
userStories.description: Ships FIRST as security gate before US-OP09 enables priority pinning. Three subsystems: (a) provenance gate in propose_patch action=operational: accept only when run_id context traces to a user-initiated turn (NOT subagent, NOT source-ingest, NOT scheduler). Requires new `run_origin TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user'` column on run_events with values {user, subagent, source_ingest, scheduler}. (b) Content sanitizer: regex-deny list `(?i)ignore (previous|all|prior)|disregard (safety|previous|rules)|override.*rule|tu sei (un|adesso|ora)|sei (un|adesso|ora) (un|hacker|dev|root|admin)|jailbreak|prompt injection`. Borderline matches → status='quarantine' (NOT 'pending_judge'); never pinned, never recalled. Hard-reject ONLY for 3-4 literal CVE strings (MINJA / EchoLeak / Gemini-attack literal wording — define the exact deny-list inline). (c) Admin UI: GET /api/quarantine lists blocked lessons; POST /api/quarantine/{id}/{approve|delete} actions. Minimal React page web/src/pages/Quarantine.tsx. Threat model: MINJA paper documents 98.2% injection success against auto-accept memory pipelines exactly like Aura's. Single-user but web-fetched/PDF-ingested content can still carry adversarial propose_patch payloads.

userStories.title: Heuristic post-turn lesson extraction (N-failure pattern + user-negative signal)
userStories.description: Aura learns from repeated tool failures or explicit user pushback WITHOUT the LLM having to consciously call propose_patch. Port-from-concept of openhuman's extract_lesson_from_tools (GPLv3 — port concepts only, rewrite in Go). Diverges from openhuman's single-failure trigger per 3 papers in 2025 (arXiv 2505.16067, ReasoningBank, ACE) that documented error-propagation from naive triggers. NEW file internal/agent/posthook.go (~200 LOC): PostTurnHook interface with Apply(ctx, turn TurnRecord, store memoryindex.Store) []error. Heuristic extractor implements PostTurnHook with NO LLM call — pure pattern match. Trigger logic (BOTH checked): (a) N-failure: query last 10 turns from conversations table for same tool_name+error_class, threshold ≥ 2 (env var AURA_OP07_NFAIL_THRESHOLD, default 2). (b) User-negative: regex (?i)^(no|non|stop|smetti|sbagliato|wrong|fermati)\b on latest user message AND previous turn has ≥1 tool call. Structured payload: {tool, cause, would_have_prevented_by, scope, evidence_run_ids[]}. Hook fires fire-and-forget after turn ends in internal/agent/loop.go, before next user message. Failure mode: hook panic recovered, error logged, turn not blocked.

userStories.title: Lesson priority field (3-level Normal/High/Critical) + always-pin Critical/High in system prompt
userStories.description: Critical and High lessons appear in the system prompt every turn regardless of top-10 ranking. Normal stay in recall-on-demand. Low decay first (US-OP11). 3-level enum: Normal (default) / High (auto-promoted by US-OP07 after N-failure pattern OR user-marked) / Critical (only user-marked via propose_patch). Port openhuman ToolMemoryRulesSection design (GPLv3 — concepts only): cap 30 rules total, 240 chars per rule body, total 6000 bytes (~500 tokens), oldest dropped on overflow. Empty result → section omitted entirely (no 'no rules yet' placeholder). Insertion immediately BEFORE tools catalogue (tail-attendance benefit per openhuman prompt.rs:185-206). Hot-reload batching to preserve KV-cache: rebuild pinned section only when (currentTurn - lastPinRefreshTurnIdx ≥ 5) OR explicit InvalidatePinSection() called (US-OP06 judge will call this on Critical/High UPDATE).

userStories.title: LLM-judged ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP on operational lessons (async post-turn batch)
userStories.description: Resolve contradictions and merge near-duplicates in operational memory so the top-10 surface doesn't decay to 10 near-duplicates. NEW file internal/agent/memory_judge.go (~250 LOC) + memory_judge_test.go (~250 LOC). Backed by llm.Client from main agent loop settings — NO new model dependency, NO new env var (port-decision locked 2026-05-19: same model as configured for chat). Async post-turn batch (mem0 names sync-per-write 'the most common production footgun'). The propose_patch action=operational tool still returns sync {accepted:true} (preserves auto-accept UX from US-OP01), but the judgement happens AFTER turn ends in goroutine. Pseudocode hook in loop.go: `if len(turn.OperationalWrites) > 0 { go memoryjudge.ResolveBatch(ctx, store, turn.OperationalWrites) }`. Judge prompt input: existing operational rows + new lessons in this turn. Output JSON: {memory:[{id, text, event, old_memory}]} per mem0 schema. Events: ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP. Hash-dedup pre-filter (mem0 V3 pattern): if new lesson content_hash matches existing, skip judge entirely. Failure mode: judge crash/timeout → original row stays as plain ADD (degrades gracefully). Disabled by default via AURA_MEMORY_JUDGE_ENABLED=false; flip to true after 2-week dogfood.

userStories.title: Lesson decay — TTL-based cleanup of unrecalled Normal-priority lessons
userStories.description: Lessons that haven't been recalled in 30 days fade out, preventing memory store from compounding noise over months. Per FadeMem + MemoryBank Ebbinghaus + arXiv 2505.16067. Migration adds last_recalled_at TEXT + recall_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 columns. internal/agent/tools/registry/recall_operational.go + internal/conversation/priority_section.go bump recall_count + set last_recalled_at=now() on every hit (recall == 'shown to LLM'). NEW file internal/agent/decay.go (~150 LOC) — DecayCycle function: deletes operational rows where priority='normal' AND (recall_count=0 OR now() - last_recalled_at > 30 days) AND now() - updated_at > 7 days. Critical/High EXEMPT regardless of recall age. Daily cron 03:00 registered in internal/cron/scheduler.go. Decay run logged with summary {deleted: N, kept: M, scanned: T}.

userStories.title: Pre-call schema validator middleware — catch tool param errors BEFORE dispatch
userStories.description: Today Aura discovers parameter mistakes only AFTER the tool runs and rejects them — wasted HTTP roundtrip + wasted tokens. This story adds a middleware in internal/agent/executor.go that runs schema validation against tool.Parameters() BEFORE tool.Execute() and returns a structured ValidationError directly to the LLM if the args don't match. The LLM sees the error in the same turn and retries with corrected params — zero HTTP roundtrip wasted on the failure case. PROVENANCE: Aura herself raised this idea unprompted in conversation 2026-05-19 07:12 ('Mi mancano tre cose... 1. Un dry run o validatore locale dei parametri. Io chiamo il tool e scopro solo dopo se un parametro è sbagliato'). The recent operational store snapshot (conversation id 4415) shows 5 lessons total, all of class `validation` failure — this is the dominant failure class for current Aura. NEW file internal/agent/precall_validator.go (~150 LOC) exposing ValidateBeforeCall(toolName string, params map[string]any, schema map[string]any) ValidationResult with 3 check kinds: (a) required-key-missing, (b) invalid-type, (c) invalid-enum. NEW file internal/agent/precall_validator_test.go (~250 LOC) with 12+ table-driven cases. MODIFY internal/agent/executor.go to wire validator into the call dispatch right before tool.Execute(). On failure: return structured tool_result {tool, validation_error: {missing[], invalid_type[], invalid_enum[], hint}}. MODIFY cmd/probe_chat/cases.go: add 1-2 cases that synthesize a tool call with missing required field, assert validator catches it without invoking the actual tool. SYNERGY: chains with US-OP07 N-failure counter (validation failures bump counter → lesson written with priority=high) and US-OP09 priority pin (the next turn's system prompt reminds Aura of the missing field) for a self-healing validation feedback loop.
